rows.ARS:
Apricot or apricot blend Hybrid Tea.
Exhibition name: Durbanville Flame
rows.Origin:
Discovered by Ludwig Taschner (South Africa, before 2001).
Introduced in South Africa by Ludwig's Roses in 2001 as 'Durbanville Flame'.
rows.Bloom: Peach - apricot, orange edges. None / no fragrance. Double (17-25 petals), high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b and warmer. Can be used for beds and borders, cut flower or garden. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that.
rows.Parentage: If you know the parentage of this rose, or other details, please contact us.
rows.Notes:
From the code name, It is presumed to be a sport.

Ludwigs Roses says Durbanville, the city just inland of Cape Town, plays host to the Rose Trials, which were established in 1979 and are maintained and evaluated through by the Municipal Parks Department and the Western Cape Rose Society...
